item.description:
Control your displays and volume from your phone.
Turn on **Control from phone** in the gear menu, press **Show QR** in the panel, and scan it with your phone's camera. The page that opens has a slider for every display, Off/25/50/100% buttons, the link toggle and the Mac's volume. It works in any phone browser — Android or iPhone — with nothing to install. Add it to your home screen to keep it one tap away.
- Only devices on your own network (or Tailscale) can connect, and every request has to carry the secret from the QR code. **New link** revokes it. - Volume follows the output device when macOS can set its level. For audio interfaces with a hardware knob, the page offers − / Mute / + buttons that press the volume keys, so apps like SoundSource pick them up. - Automation apps such as HTTP Shortcuts can use the same API; see the README.
The panel now always opens directly below the menu bar, on the screen whose icon you clicked. With a monitor arranged above the laptop it used to open half off-screen, and it no longer slides away with an auto-hiding menu bar.

The interface is now in English.
Every string the app shows — the panel, the gear menu, the permission warning, the display names and the `--diagnose` report — was Turkish and is now English. The calibration summary distinguishes "1 point" from "3 points" rather than reusing a single form.
Source comments remain Turkish; identifiers and UI text are uniformly English.
This release was built and published by CI rather than by hand.

First public release.
- Per-display brightness sliders for the built-in panel and DDC/CI monitors. - `F1`/`F2` drive both displays together through a calibration curve you teach it. - True black on external monitors: gamma dimming below DDC zero, then backlight off. - On-screen HUD, hot-plug and sleep handling, `--diagnose` troubleshooting mode. - Signed and notarized, with automatic updates.
